blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail to greet by name) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message, e.g. `throw new NotFoundError("no customer with that e-mail")`. The route hands the error to `errorHandler` (src/routes.ts:9 `next(error);`), which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })` (src/server.ts), so every lookup that misses — a typo, a former customer, a person who never was one — writes the typed e-mail address to the application log, where it has no retention rule and escapes erasure (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) and 5(1)(e)). Add a test asserting the logged message does not contain the address.
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that the Helply widget "greets the signed-in customer by name, so that the agent knows who they talk to": send only `id` and `name` to the widget, and drop `email`, `phone`, `birthDate` and `address`. As written, `GET /chat/settings` exposes the whole record to the browser and to the third-party Helply SDK for every signed-in customer, whether or not they ever open a chat — data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)) and sharing with a processor beyond the purpose (Art. 28). Also narrow the `customerById` SELECT to the columns used.
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date, address and e-mail to greet by name

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The proposal says agents look a customer up so they need not ask "who they are"; it does not state why an agent needs the birth date or postal address. Either return only the fields the support workflow needs (id, name, e-mail) or state in the proposal the purpose that requires the rest (e.g. identity verification). Whether agents need them is for the team to confirm (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)).
findings.title: Support lookup returns birth date and address with no stated need

findings.recommendation: The change starts sending customer data to Helply, but the plan does not name it as a processor nor say where it hosts data (inside or outside the EEA), nor whether a processing agreement covers it and what retention it applies (GDPR Art. 28, Art. 30, Chapter V). A question for the team: record the processor, its location and lawful basis in the proposal.
findings.title: Helply as a new processor is not identified
